transcript.text:
Try these safe checks first:

1. Power
• Make sure it’s plugged in firmly.
• Check the wall socket, fuse/breaker, and try another appliance in that socket.
• If it has a delay/start button, hold Start for a few seconds—many dryers need this rather than a quick press.

2. Door and load
• Close the door firmly; check nothing is caught in the latch.
• Don’t overfill it. Try a small load.

3. Clean airflow
• Clean the lint filter completely.
• Check the vent hose/outside vent for kinks or blockage.
• For condenser/heat-pump dryers, empty the water tank and clean the condenser/filter if applicable.
• Poor airflow can make the dryer stop heating or cut out on overheating protection.

4. If it runs but doesn’t heat
• Check it isn’t set to air/fluff/no-heat mode.
• Clean filters and vents, then allow it to cool for 30 minutes and retry.
• If still cold, likely causes include a heater element, thermal fuse/thermostat, or control fault—usually a repair job.

5. If it won’t start at all
• Check the door switch/latch and power supply.
• A humming noise without drum movement can indicate a belt, motor, or capacitor issue.

6. Stop using it and arrange repair if
• You smell burning, see smoke, hear scraping/banging, the plug/socket gets hot, or it repeatedly trips the breaker.
• For a gas dryer, turn it off and don’t investigate internally if you smell gas.

Tell me the make/model and exactly what it does—e.g. no power, drum won’t turn, turns but no heat, stops mid-cycle, or displays an error code—and I can narrow it down.
It's a Hotpoint condenser. Lights come on but nothing happens when I press start, no sound at all and the drum doesn't turn. Door had felt loose for a few days.

The loose door strongly suggests the door catch/interlock switch isn’t being engaged, so the dryer thinks the door is open and will not start. This is a common reason for lights to work but no motor sound or drum movement.

Try this:

1. Unplug the dryer first.
2. Check the door:
• Look for a broken, loose, or missing plastic/metal catch tab on the door edge.
• Check the slot/lock in the dryer front where the door clicks shut. Remove lint/debris carefully.
• Check whether the door has dropped on its hinges or needs lifting slightly to close.
3. Plug it back in and, while pressing the door firmly shut—sometimes gently lifting the door as well—press and hold Start for 2–3 seconds.
4. Make sure the water container is emptied and fully pushed back in, and that the filter is seated properly. These usually give an indicator, but it is worth checking.
5. If a padlock/child-lock symbol is lit, disable it; on many Hotpoint models this involves holding two marked buttons together for a few seconds.

If it starts only when you push, lift, or hold the door in a particular position, the likely fault is the door latch, catch, hinge alignment, or door interlock switch. It needs replacement/adjustment rather than bypassing—the interlock is a safety device.

Do not try to defeat or bridge the door switch. If the door will not click securely closed, leave the dryer unplugged until repaired.

If you can give the full Hotpoint model number from the label inside the door or on the rear, I can tell you the likely interlock/catch arrangement and the relevant checks for that model.

No click when I shut it, the door swings back slightly open. The plastic tongue on the door has snapped off, I found the piece on the floor. If I hold the door shut and press start it runs, but it stops when I let go. Water container is in properly and child lock isn't on. I don't know the model number offhand, I can go and look for it if you need it.

That confirms it: the door striker/catch tongue has broken off. The dryer is behaving correctly—the safety interlock only allows it to run while the door is held closed.

Do not keep using it by holding the door shut or attempt to bypass the switch. Unplug it until the catch is repaired.

You will most likely need a replacement door catch/striker—sometimes supplied as part of the inner door frame/door handle assembly, depending on the Hotpoint model. Avoid gluing the broken piece back on: it is under repeated load and heat, so it is unlikely to be a safe or lasting repair.

The model number will be needed to identify the correct part. On a Hotpoint condenser dryer, look for the rating plate:

• around the inside of the door opening / door rim;
• on the inside face of the door;
• or on the rear panel.

Take a photo of the label if possible. The useful details are the model number and ideally the industrial/service code (often begins with something like 85… or 86…).

Once you have that, I can help identify whether the broken part is a separately replaceable striker or whether it needs a door assembly component.
ok, I'll go and read the label inside the door recess now. I haven't got the number yet though.

No problem. Look for a label with wording such as Model, Mod., Type, Service, Industrial code, or an 85/86… number.

When you have it, send either:

• the full model number, or
• a clear photo/transcription of everything on the label.

The key is to match the replacement door catch/striker to the exact model.
ok, still looking for the label inside the door recess, will send it when I find it

Take your time. Keep the dryer unplugged while the door catch is broken.

When you find the label, send the model number and any service/industrial code shown; that will be enough to identify the right door catch part.
